concepts.def: Fictional industrial town just before WW1.
Working-class woman whose death links the family.
Central theme: 'we are members of one body'.
The play attacks privilege and indifference.

walkthroughs.body_html: Priestley sets the play in 1912 but wrote it in 1945. His 1945 audience knew the World Wars and the Depression had punctured Edwardian confidence. Birling's boasts about the Titanic and a peaceful future arrive as dramatic irony from the moment the curtain rises.

The Inspector interrogates Arthur, Sybil, Sheila, Eric, and Gerald Croft. Each contributed to Eva Smith's death: dismissal, jealousy, exploitation, abandonment, charity refused. Priestley constructs a chain so that no single villain can absorb the blame.

The Inspector's final speech tells the family 'we are members of one body' and warns of 'fire and blood and anguish' if the lesson is not learned. Priestley's 1945 audience hear the lesson through two World Wars - and through the new welfare state's promises.
